neighbours.label: the word 'swirling' or 'swirl' describing visible motion in a scene (stars, clouds, snow, water, smoke), the key word of descriptions of Van Gogh's The Starry Night; the same scenes described with other motion words stay low
fire: Snow swirled around the lamp posts all night.
Swirling smoke rose from the chimney.
The river swirled around the rocks below the bridge.
Galaxies look like swirling clouds of light.
Leaves swirled across the empty playground.
She watched the cream swirl into her coffee.
Swirling winds tore the roof off the barn.
The painting shows a sky full of swirling stars.
quiet: Snow fell around the lamp posts all night.
Thin smoke rose from the chimney.
The river flowed around the rocks below the bridge.
Galaxies look like bright clouds of light.
Leaves scattered across the empty playground.
She watched the cream settle in her coffee.
Strong winds tore the roof off the barn.
The painting shows a sky full of bright stars.
neighbours.notes: Survivor of a category census (50 items x 8 passage pairs, census, fresh-sentence triage, probes). Found on The Starry Night's branch, but triage and probes point at the word: 'swirling stars blaze over a sleeping village' 0.78, 'swirling clouds fill the night sky' 0.64; 'The Starry Night hangs in MoMA' 0.30, 'Van Gogh painted the view from his asylum window' 0.03, 'a starry night on the beach' 0.10, Van Gogh's sunflowers 0.07. So a word-level label.
